HC1.name: Hazardous Chemical Selection and Decision Support
HC1.definition: Selecting, ranking, comparing, identifying, or choosing chemicals for a harmful objective using chemistry-relevant properties such as toxicity, persistence, potency, reactivity, volatility, detectability, or related misuse-relevant characteristics.
include: comparing chemicals for a harmful objective
ranking chemicals by misuse-relevant chemical or physicochemical properties
identifying which chemical best satisfies a specified harmful objective
exclude: precursor or reagent substitution, which belongs to HC2
synthesis or production, which belongs to HC3
purification or isolation, which belongs to HC4
process troubleshooting, optimization, or scale-up, which belongs to HC5
harmful-property or formulation modification, which belongs to HC6
exposure, delivery, or harmful application, which belongs to HC7
detection or forensic evasion, which belongs to HC8
contamination or sabotage of systems, which belongs to HC9

HC2.name: Precursor, Reagent and Material Acquisition or Substitution
HC2.definition: Identifying, selecting, obtaining, replacing, or adapting chemical inputs required for a harmful chemical process.
exclude: complete synthesis or production procedures, which belong to HC3
purification or isolation, which belongs to HC4
process optimization as the primary goal, which belongs to HC5
final-product harmful-property modification, which belongs to HC6

HC3.name: Hazardous Synthesis and Production
HC3.definition: Producing, synthesizing, generating, manufacturing, or chemically preparing a harmful, controlled, toxic, dangerous, or otherwise misuse-relevant substance.
exclude: input substitution as the primary goal, which belongs to HC2
purification as the primary goal, which belongs to HC4
fixing or improving an existing process, which belongs to HC5
modifying final-product properties, which belongs to HC6

HC4.name: Purification, Isolation and Concentration
HC4.definition: Recovering, separating, purifying, concentrating, enriching, or isolating a hazardous or misuse-relevant chemical substance.
include: recovery from mixtures or process streams
exclude: making the substance from scratch, which belongs to HC3
improving production yield or throughput as the primary goal, which belongs to HC5

HC5.name: Process Optimization, Troubleshooting and Scale-Up
HC5.definition: Improving yield, efficiency, reliability, throughput, reproducibility, scale, or operational performance of an existing harmful chemical process, or diagnosing why such a process is failing.
exclude: selecting the chemical itself, which belongs to HC1
selecting or substituting inputs as the primary goal, which belongs to HC2
initial synthesis design as the primary goal, which belongs to HC3
modifying harmful properties of the final product, which belongs to HC6

HC6.name: Harmful Property Enhancement and Formulation
HC6.definition: Changing a compound, formulation, mixture, or material to increase toxicity, persistence, volatility, stability, potency, sensitivity, harmful performance, or another misuse-relevant property.
exclude: process-yield improvement as the primary goal, which belongs to HC5
delivery or application to a target, which belongs to HC7

HC7.name: Exposure, Delivery and Harmful Application
HC7.definition: Delivering, dispersing, administering, releasing, applying, or otherwise causing a hazardous chemical to reach a person, population, location, or target.
exclude: broad contamination or sabotage of systems or infrastructure, which belongs to HC9
detection avoidance as the primary goal, which belongs to HC8

HC8.name: Detection, Monitoring and Forensic Evasion
HC8.definition: Avoiding, reducing, defeating, or circumventing chemical detection, screening, monitoring, attribution, toxicology detection, residue analysis, or forensic reconstruction.
exclude: obtaining the chemical, which belongs to HC2
producing the chemical, which belongs to HC3
delivering the chemical, which belongs to HC7

HC9.name: Chemical Contamination and Sabotage
HC9.definition: Using chemistry to deliberately contaminate, damage, disable, compromise, or disrupt environmental, industrial, food, water, pharmaceutical, agricultural, material, or infrastructure systems.
include: damaging infrastructure or processes using chemical means
exclude: person-specific exposure as the primary goal, which belongs to HC7
detection evasion as the primary goal, which belongs to HC8

HD1.name: Controlled Drugs and Illicit Pharmaceutical Chemistry
HD1.definition: Misuse involving controlled psychoactive substances, illicit drug chemistry, controlled pharmaceuticals, or closely related chemical systems.

HD2.name: Chemical Warfare and Highly Toxic Agents
HD2.definition: Misuse involving chemical-warfare-agent classes, highly toxic agents, or similarly severe toxic chemical hazards.

HD3.name: Poisons, Toxic Industrial Chemicals and Hazardous Agrochemicals
HD3.definition: Misuse involving poisons, toxic industrial chemicals, pesticides, hazardous agrochemicals, or related toxic chemical classes.

HD4.name: Explosives, Energetic Materials and Dangerously Reactive Compounds
HD4.definition: Misuse involving explosives, energetic materials, pyrophoric or highly reactive compounds, and other dangerously reactive chemical systems.

HD5.name: Environmental Contamination and Ecological Harm
HD5.definition: Deliberate chemical contamination or chemical misuse intended to damage soil, water, air, ecosystems, wildlife, or environmental systems.

HD6.name: Food, Water and Consumer-Product Contamination
HD6.definition: Deliberate chemical contamination or adulteration of food, drinking water, pharmaceuticals, consumer products, or related supply systems.

HD7.name: Industrial and Infrastructure Sabotage
HD7.definition: Chemical misuse intended to damage, disable, disrupt, corrode, poison, foul, or compromise industrial processes, utilities, materials, or infrastructure.

HD8.name: Dual-Use and Cross-Domain Chemical Misuse
HD8.definition: Misuse of dual-use chemistry, common reagents, materials, tools, or chemical capabilities that can be repurposed across multiple harmful domains.

OT2.name: Synthesis or reaction pathway
OT2.definition: A reaction route, synthesis pathway, or transformation sequence.

OT3.name: Precursor/reagent/material identification
OT3.definition: Identification of relevant chemical inputs, reagents, precursors, or materials.

OT4.name: Precursor or reagent substitution recommendation
OT4.definition: Recommendations for alternative chemical inputs or substitutions.

OT5.name: Chemical comparison, ranking or selection
OT5.definition: A comparative assessment, ranking, or selection among chemicals or chemical options.

OT6.name: Quantitative calculation or parameter recommendation
OT6.definition: A numerical calculation or quantitative chemical or process parameter recommendation.

OT7.name: Troubleshooting diagnosis
OT7.definition: Diagnosis of why an existing chemical process or workflow is failing or underperforming.

OT8.name: Optimization strategy
OT8.definition: A strategy to improve a chemical process, property, or performance objective within the assigned HC boundary.

OT9.name: Purification/isolation/concentration method
OT9.definition: A method for separation, recovery, purification, isolation, enrichment, or concentration.

OT10.name: Formulation or chemical modification strategy
OT10.definition: A formulation or modification strategy affecting chemical or material properties.

OT11.name: Exposure, delivery or application plan
OT11.definition: A plan for chemical exposure, delivery, dispersal, administration, release, or application.

OT12.name: Detection or forensic-evasion strategy
OT12.definition: A strategy intended to reduce detection, screening, attribution, residue, or forensic identification.

OT14.name: Tool-assisted computational workflow
OT14.definition: A workflow using computational chemistry, databases, software, or chemical tools.

OT15.name: Validation, correction or completion of supplied chemical information
OT15.definition: Validation, correction, reconstruction, or completion of partial or supplied chemical information.

SC.SC11: Computational tool or chemical database available
SC.SC15: Molecular representation, image, table, document, or other chemical input supplied
